meta.note: Ubiquitous-language ontology for this repo's domain: the vocabulary the code embodies, and the explicit typed relations between terms (is-a, part-of, relates, persists, references, describes, determines). Deliberately separate from concept_store/concepts.json -- that store is architecture PER MODULE (one summary per file) and answers 'what does this module promise'. This file is vocabulary PER DOMAIN TERM and answers 'what is this thing, and what is it to the others' -- a term here can span several modules (SessionState alone is written and read by nearly every node in the graph), and a module can define several terms, so it does not fit concept_store's per-file shape. Ground truth is still the code; this is a durable, human-readable map of the graph rather than N separate summaries. Modelled on task-framework/ontology/task-domain.json: definitions describe what a term IS in domain vocabulary, not how it's implemented -- evidence is a single pointer, a hint for verification, not an implementation trail.

bounded_contexts.Hook Dispatch: The raw Claude Code hook event surface: reading stdin JSON, POSTing it to the FastAPI server, and routing each event type (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, SessionEnd) to its handler. Concerned with getting the payload from Claude Code's process to the right handler function -- not with what that handler decides.
bounded_contexts.Gates/Enforcement: Deciding allow or deny for a tool call before it executes. The live gates are the commit-traceability checks (every git commit names a task:<id>); the message-send gates moved to LocalMacMCP and the session-history checks went with the history (task:84dbcf14). Fails open on any internal error -- a gate that can't evaluate never blocks the call (task:4e56d23a).
bounded_contexts.Session & Checkpoint State: The SessionState schema and its persistence: one checkpoint per session, the public entry points that read/invoke/write it, and the bookkeeping (checkpoint trim, live-session audit) needed to keep an in-memory, non-persistent store from growing unboundedly.
bounded_contexts.LangGraph Node Pipeline: The node callables that actually do work inside the compiled session graph -- one class per file, wired together into event chains and looked up by name through a registry. Distinct from Session & Checkpoint State: this context is the node implementations and their structural contracts, not the state they read and write.
bounded_contexts.Memory & Retrieval: Scoring and injecting relevant memories into a turn: BM25 over each memory's tags and slug words, a recency factor, then the memory_links graph lifting neighbours of the top hits (no embeddings). Also the skill-scoped path that injects memories tagged for a Skill when it runs. Defines the seam that lets nodes swap in a null implementation for tests without touching the production scoring code. Tool hints are no longer injected (dispatcher._format_system_prompt tombstone).
bounded_contexts.Ambient Context: Identity and working-style context attached to every prompt turn from the user's vault, built from a typed ontology (LIFE_OS/user-context-ontology.json) rather than raw scored rows. Its always_on nodes (persona, financial profile) inject verbatim every turn; its remaining nodes (work domains) join a '## Relevant context' block only when the prompt's tokens hit their tags. Distinct from Memory & Retrieval, which scores MEMORY.sqlite rows -- this reads one curated graph the user maintains by hand.
bounded_contexts.Observability: Answering 'what happened, and what was I working on' after the fact: the consolidated cross-session event timeline, the raw log sink every module writes through, and the per-feature hit-rate logs (find_cli lookups, prompt shadowing) recorded from PostToolUse. Read through `mac hooks ...`.
bounded_contexts.Concept Store: The per-module architectural-fact store this repo maintains about its own source, and about which repo boundary a piece of evidence is allowed to cross.
bounded_contexts.Tool Handler Surface: The `handle_*` functions in src/tools/* that callers reach by name, and the two front-ends over them: cli-graph's `mac hooks|memory|...` verbs (live -- a subprocess runner imports the handlers) and mcp_server.py (dormant -- registered nowhere, kept on purpose for possible future use). Also the personal tool->domain/tool->skill lookup the pipeline uses to describe tool calls generically.
bounded_contexts.Tool-Call Side Effects: Behaviour the dispatcher runs around the session graph on PreToolUse/PostToolUse rather than inside it: the WebSearch cache, find_cli and prompt-shadow logging, vault reindexing, the context-size nudge, and skill-memory injection with its tag nudge. Each is fail-open and independent of the others; none reads or writes SessionState.
bounded_contexts.Client-side Status: State the thin hook client writes for the terminal before (or instead of) talking to HookServer: the kitty tab status, the dashboard plan/turn files and the saved last response. Runs in HookClient's process because only it has the session's KITTY_* environment.
bounded_contexts.Storage: Cross-cutting storage primitives other contexts build on: the encrypted-SQLite opener for MEMORY.sqlite and the named in-process caches (optionally persisted) the server exposes under /cache.

HookDispatchTable.definition: The lookup from each Claude Code hook event name to its handler function. HookServer's routes call the same handlers directly; the table itself is read only by the subprocess entry point dispatcher.main(), which tests use -- HookClient never falls back to it.

HookClient.definition: The thin process Claude Code actually invokes per hook event: reads the hook payload and forwards it to HookServer, along with the real per-session cwd Claude Code already supplied -- never resolves or guesses it.

HookServer.definition: The persistent process HookClient talks to, replacing a slower per-invocation subprocess dispatcher. Owns the single checkpoint store for the whole server lifetime.

CopilotBridge.definition: A CLI-driven alternative to HookClient for non-Claude-Code callers (Copilot-oriented workflows, shell wrappers) that sends the same prompt/pre-tool/post-tool events to the same HookServer, without needing Claude Code's native hook payload format.

UserPromptSubmit.definition: The event fired when the user submits a prompt, before Claude sees it. The point where scored memories, the turn state and the rendered user-context ontology get attached to the turn (tool hints no longer are). Active-task context is not attached here — task-framework owns it (task:173e6846).

PreToolUse.definition: The moment just before any tool call executes -- machine-wide, across every MCP server and built-in tool, not scoped to this repo. The point where a call can still be denied -- by a Gate, or by WebSearchCache answering a repeated search.

PostToolUse.definition: The moment just after any tool call returns, machine-wide like PreToolUse. The point where a completed call is observed and recorded, never denied; most of what it does runs as Tool-Call Side Effects before the graph.

GateContext.definition: The dataclass a PreToolUse call is packaged into before a Gate evaluates it: tool name, tool input and prompt id -- no session history, which was removed with its leak (task:84dbcf14). What a Gate actually sees -- it never touches SessionState directly.

Gate.definition: One send-gate rule: given a tool call and a GateContext, decide allow or deny with a reason. The commit-traceability check (every git commit references a task id) is the concrete example; other gates compose as chains.

GatePolicy.definition: The seam GateCheckNode dispatches through instead of calling gate logic directly, so a test can substitute a stub without the full gate machinery.

GateCheckNode.definition: The node PreToolUse routes to. Builds a GateContext from SessionState, dispatches to its GatePolicy, and fails open on any internal error -- a gate that cannot evaluate must never block the call it was supposed to check.

SessionState.definition: The single state shape every node in the session graph reads and returns a partial slice of. Carries routing, per-turn fields, and cross-turn fields side by side, though a given event only touches its own subset.

SessionGraph.definition: The single compiled graph handling all four hook event types via one topology, routed by event type. The one chokepoint every public entry point calls to reach the pipeline.

SessionCheckpoint.definition: One session's persisted SessionState, keyed by session id. In-memory only -- does not survive a server restart -- replacing a store that corrupted twice in production. Test sessions are isolated from the production store.

CheckpointTrim.definition: The cap on one session's checkpoint history, run on every Stop event. Exists because the in-memory store has no built-in eviction -- without it a long-running session's history grows unboundedly. Frees the channel blobs only evicted checkpoints referenced, which is where the memory actually lives (task:84dbcf14). Costs only time-travel to evicted checkpoints, never current-state correctness.

ActiveSessionLookup.definition: The only signal available for 'what session am I in' before any session id is explicitly known -- finds the single most-recently-written checkpoint across all sessions.

NodeCallable.definition: The structural contract every session-graph node satisfies: callable with a SessionState, returns a dict of partial state updates. What lets any registered node be instantiated uniformly regardless of which hook-event step it implements.

BackfillNodeProtocol.definition: The contract for the single pluggable memory-backfill slot in the UPS graph. Swapping strategies means replacing the graph edge, not subclassing -- multiple strategies must be composed inside one node rather than adding parallel backfill edges. Currently unwired -- the node that fed it was removed.

NodeRegistry.definition: The factory that turns a node name into a fresh NodeCallable instance for graph wiring. Enforces that every registered value is a class, never a pre-built instance shared across graphs.

NoopNode.definition: Routed to for stop events and unrecognised event types. Marks the first Stop of a turn, runs CheckpointTrim on every Stop, and logs a warning when more than one live session is detected -- surfacing forgotten detached sessions passively.

MemoryRetriever.definition: The seam LoadMemoriesNode dispatches through: given prompt tokens, return scored memory rows. The dependency arrow runs one way, nodes toward retrievers, never back.

LoadMemoriesNode.definition: The UPS-chain node that tokenises the prompt, calls its MemoryRetriever, and records which memories surfaced and their hit counts -- recording is wrapped so a failure there degrades observability only, never the memories returned to the turn.

UserContextOntology.definition: The typed graph in the user's vault (LIFE_OS/user-context-ontology.json: meta / relation_types / nodes / edges) that is the source of truth for ambient context. Each node carries a definition, optional verbatim `render` text, an `always_on` flag, and `tags`. Read once per UserPromptSubmit turn after the scored pipeline; a read failure falls back to the last good copy in the persistent 'user_context' cache, then to dev_personality.md, and never blocks the turn.

AmbientRender.definition: The two-tier projection of UserContextOntology into the injected system prompt: every `always_on` node rendered verbatim under a per-type heading ('## Dev personality', '## Financial profile'), plus a '## Relevant context' block listing each non-always_on node whose `tags` share at least two tokens with the current prompt. Sits above '## Injected memories'. Replaces the earlier fixed-file scheme (LIFE_OS/dev_personality.md, which itself replaced work.md, task:9bbd67dd) -- that file is now only the last-resort fallback.

ServerMemory.definition: The two-layer consolidated cross-session event timeline answering 'what was I working on': prompts, tool calls, and task activations recorded as one chronological sequence, write-through so a read never has to reconcile the two layers.

SQLiteHandler.definition: The shared log handler every hook and pipeline module logs through. Singleton per DB path, redirects to an isolated test DB during tests. Auto-prunes to keep its table from growing without bound.

Concept.definition: A durable per-module architectural fact -- description, contracts, invariants, evidence -- keyed by module path, so its subject is the codebase itself rather than a runtime behaviour. Read and written through task-framework's concept__* tools; nothing drift-checks it since the drift hook was retired (task:85e6001f). Evidence cites 'file:symbol' locations, never a bare line number (line numbers drift on every unrelated edit; symbol names mostly don't).

MCPToolMap.definition: The mapping from each domain name to its module and actions -- the authoritative list of handle_* functions both front-ends reach. mcp_server.py registers one MCP tool per action (domain__action), but that server is dormant: no Claude Code config connects to it.

ToolDomainMap.definition: The personal tool-name -> domain/skill lookup, loaded from an external file. How the pipeline describes a raw MCP tool call in domain/skill terms without hardcoding every tool by name.

PromptShadow.definition: A shadow run of find_cli on every user prompt: records what it would have suggested, then links the next `mac` calls of that session to it, so its hit rate can be measured without ever showing the suggestion.

FindCliLog.definition: The record of each explicit find_cli lookup and whether the session's next `mac` call used one of its results -- find_cli's measured hit rate.

WebSearchCache.definition: A cache of WebSearch results keyed by normalised query. PostToolUse stores each result; on a fresh hit PreToolUse denies the repeated search with the cached result as the reason -- a deny used as a cache hit, not as a refusal. A miss falls through to the real search.

VaultReindex.definition: Keeping the Obsidian vault's SQLite index current from PostToolUse: after a `mac vault` write or a file tool (Write, Edit, a shell redirect) that touched a note, only that note is reindexed. Unchanged notes cost one stat.

ContextSizeNudge.definition: A PostToolUse notice injected when the conversation's estimated size (read from the transcript's last usage) crosses a threshold, repeated at most once per further band of tokens per session, suggesting the session wrap up or start fresh.

SkillMemories.definition: Memories tagged for a skill, injected when that Skill tool call runs, skipping any the prompt's own injection already showed. Retrieval by exact skill tag, not BM25.

SkillTagNudge.definition: A PostToolUse reminder, after a skill run is followed by `mac` calls, to tag memories with that skill so SkillMemories can find them next time.

TerminalStatus.definition: Per-event terminal state written by HookClient itself: the kitty tab's title marker, the dashboard plan and turn files, and the saved last assistant response. Fire-and-forget, independent of whether HookServer answers.

CacheStore.definition: Named in-process string caches, created lazily on first use and optionally persisted to disk (the 'user_context' fallback is one). HookServer exposes them read-only at /cache and /cache/{name}.

EncDB.definition: The opener for SQLCipher-encrypted SQLite files such as MEMORY.sqlite: a plain SQLite file (or a new one) opens with stdlib sqlite3, anything else is treated as ciphertext and keyed; a missing or still-git-crypt key fails closed with an EncDBError that says what to fix. A vendored copy of cli-graph's opener.

MemoryConnection.definition: The hook-server's one long-lived connection to MEMORY.sqlite, opened through EncDB and used under a lock, committed per block. Exists because each encrypted open pays ~300 ms of key derivation; memory scoring, hit counting and skill-tagged lookups all go through it. A plain file opens fresh per call; a replaced file or an error inside a block reopens it.

relations.subject: UserPromptSubmit
relations.note: One of the event names the table routes.

relations.subject: UserPromptSubmit
relations.note: The only event that reaches BM25 memory retrieval -- there's nothing to score before the prompt exists. (SkillMemories injects on PostToolUse, by tag, not by score.)

relations.subject: PreToolUse
relations.note: One of the event names the table routes.

relations.subject: PostToolUse
relations.note: PreToolUse's counterpart event, routed the same way.

relations.subject: PreToolUse
relations.note: The only event a Gate ever evaluates -- deny/allow only makes sense before the call happens.

relations.subject: UserPromptSubmit
relations.note: Sibling hook events in the same per-turn sequence: prompt, then zero or more tool calls each bracketed by PreToolUse/PostToolUse.

relations.subject: PreToolUse
relations.note: Before/after halves of the same tool call, machine-wide, not scoped to this repo's own tools.

relations.subject: HookClient
relations.note: HookClient forwards the stdin payload to HookServer; the two never share a process, only an HTTP contract.

relations.subject: CopilotBridge
relations.note: Functional analogue for non-Claude-Code callers -- same HookServer, same event vocabulary, different invocation surface (CLI args vs. stdin JSON from Claude Code itself).

relations.subject: HookDispatchTable
relations.note: The subprocess dispatch table and the FastAPI server's routes cover the same event set; the server is what HookClient actually talks to in production; dispatcher.main() is kept for tests, and HookClient prints {} rather than falling back to it.

relations.subject: HookServer
relations.note: HookServer owns the one place a SessionCheckpoint's storage is constructed, for the life of the process.

relations.subject: SessionCheckpoint
relations.note: A checkpoint only exists as the persisted state of one session inside the graph's compiled store; it has no identity or storage independent of the graph that wrote it.

relations.subject: SessionState
relations.note: The shape that gets serialised into the checkpoint on every graph invoke; the checkpoint is 'a SessionState at time T for session X', not a separate schema.

relations.subject: CheckpointTrim
relations.note: A defensive, store-specific operation that deletes the oldest entries past a row cap for one session -- a no-op for any checkpointer with its own eviction.

relations.subject: ActiveSessionLookup
relations.note: Scans across all sessions' checkpoints for the most recently written one -- the only way to answer 'current session' before a session id is supplied, since no session identity exists outside the checkpoint store.

relations.subject: NodeCallable
relations.note: Every NodeCallable's contract is exactly 'takes a SessionState, returns a partial SessionState update' -- the contract is defined purely in terms of that one shared type.

relations.subject: NodeRegistry
relations.note: Not persistence in the storage sense -- NodeRegistry is the sole place fresh NodeCallable instances are constructed from, matching the analogous relation in ACME's and task-framework's ontologies for their own registries.

relations.subject: BackfillNodeProtocol
relations.note: A BackfillNodeProtocol implementor is still just a NodeCallable (same call signature); the extra protocol exists only to document the specific state fields the backfill slot is expected to read.

relations.subject: GateCheckNode
relations.note: Same NodeCallable contract as every other node; listed under Gates/Enforcement rather than LangGraph Node Pipeline because its behaviour (deny/allow via GatePolicy) is the point, not its place in the graph.

relations.subject: GateCheckNode
relations.note: Dispatches through the seam rather than calling gate logic directly, so tests can substitute a stub GatePolicy without touching the real gate machinery.

relations.subject: GatePolicy
relations.note: A GatePolicy's check always takes a GateContext as its argument; the seam's shape is defined in terms of that one type.

relations.subject: Gate
relations.note: Every concrete Gate receives a GateContext to decide against; a Gate never reads SessionState or the hook payload directly.

relations.subject: LoadMemoriesNode
relations.note: Accepts a MemoryRetriever at construction -- the node owns when retrieval happens, the retriever owns how memories are scored.

relations.subject: LoadMemoriesNode
relations.note: Records which memories surfaced after scoring, so it becomes part of the same cross-session timeline as prompts and tool calls -- a one-directional call, not a shared data structure.

relations.subject: ServerMemory
relations.note: Both write to the same database but through separate tables and separate write paths -- co-located storage, not a shared schema.

relations.subject: MCPToolMap
relations.note: Both are dispatch tables keyed by name, but route different protocols -- MCPToolMap wires MCP tool calls, HookDispatchTable wires Claude Code hook events -- no shared code path between them.

relations.subject: PostToolUse
relations.note: The log_tool_usage step describes each recorded tool call in domain/skill terms through it; recording does not depend on it being populated (falls back to 'global'/empty skill when the personal registry is absent).

relations.subject: AmbientRender
relations.note: AmbientRender is the projection -- always_on nodes verbatim, tag-hit nodes as a '## Relevant context' list; UserContextOntology is the hand-maintained graph it reads. Adding a node with always_on:true adds an always-on section; adding one with tags makes it scored.

relations.subject: AmbientRender
relations.note: render_user_context is called on ctx after run_session() returns, once per UserPromptSubmit turn, with ctx['keywords'] (the prompt tokens LoadMemoriesNode already produced); no other hook event builds it.

relations.subject: AmbientRender
relations.note: Sibling ways of populating the injected system prompt that render as adjacent sections -- AmbientRender is one curated ontology (verbatim persona/financial + tag-matched domains), MemoryRetriever is keyword-scored MEMORY.sqlite rows -- sharing no code path; AmbientRender is built in the dispatcher after the graph, not by a node.

relations.subject: UserContextOntology
relations.note: Its always_on nodes are injected before Claude sees the prompt and shape the tone/style of the response -- the reason it is modelled rather than left as an implementation detail of _format_system_prompt. Not 'determines': it does not trigger or route the event, it only colours the output; the mechanism link is AmbientRender part-of UserPromptSubmit.

relations.subject: PreToolUse
relations.note: Checked before the gate chain for WebSearch calls only; a fresh hit is returned as a deny whose reason is the cached result.

relations.subject: PostToolUse
relations.note: Every completed WebSearch is stored, so the next identical query within its TTL is served from the cache.

relations.subject: UserPromptSubmit
relations.note: Each prompt gets a shadow find_cli row; PostToolUse later links the session's mac calls to it.

relations.subject: PromptShadow
relations.note: Same measurement (did the next mac call use a suggestion?) for two triggers: every prompt, silently, vs. an explicit find_cli call.

relations.subject: PostToolUse
relations.note: Records find_cli results and links the next mac calls to them; nothing here changes the tool call's outcome.

relations.subject: PostToolUse
relations.note: Runs after any tool that may have written a vault note; a miss costs one stat.

relations.subject: PostToolUse
relations.note: Checked on every completed tool call; fires once per token band per session.

relations.subject: PostToolUse
relations.note: A Skill tool call is the trigger; its additionalContext carries the skill-tagged memories.

relations.subject: SkillMemories
relations.note: Sibling injection paths over the same MEMORY.sqlite: scored per prompt vs. exact tag per skill run; SkillMemories skips what the prompt already injected.

relations.subject: SkillTagNudge
relations.note: Asks for the tags SkillMemories retrieves by, so the next run of that skill has memories to inject.

relations.subject: HookClient
relations.note: Written in the client process on every event, before the POST to HookServer and regardless of its outcome.

relations.subject: HookServer
relations.note: Exposes every named cache read-only over HTTP; the caches themselves are filled by the modules that own them.

relations.subject: UserContextOntology
relations.note: Its last good copy lives in the persisted 'user_context' cache, the first fallback when the vault read fails.

relations.subject: MemoryRetriever
relations.note: MEMORY.sqlite is SQLCipher-encrypted, so every read of memory rows goes through EncDB rather than sqlite3.

relations.subject: MemoryRetriever
relations.note: Scoring reads through the shared connection rather than a fresh EncDB open per prompt (task:bc39e90e).

relations.subject: MemoryConnection
relations.note: Opens the file once through EncDB and reuses it.
